package.name: tavus
package.packageFile:
# TAVUS — a live talking face for a page.
#
# THE FACE, NOT THE BRAIN. Tavus runs the call on its own servers: it listens, sees, takes turns and
# renders the face. What the face knows comes from the PAL configured in Tavus and the tools that PAL
# is given there, which is where an MCP connector to our own /mcp goes. Nothing about the persona is
# copied into this package: the PAL lives in Tavus and the node only names it.

name: tavus
displayName: Tavus
description: Live video conversations with an AI face
version: 1.0.0
category: communication

features:
  - Start a live video conversation with a PAL and hand its link to a page

allowedHosts:
  - tavusapi.com

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.6.0"
  credential: [apiKeyHeader]
  transport: [json]

credentials.tavusCredential.yaml:
name: tavusCredential
displayName: Tavus
description: Tavus API key for starting live video conversations

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Tavus API key, from the API Keys page of the Tavus dashboard
    placeholder: Enter your Tavus API key

files.api/events.yaml:
- emit: conversationUrl
  value: "return response.conversation_url"

- emit: conversationId
  value: "return response.conversation_id"
files.api/run.yaml:
# ONE CALL. Tavus answers the POST with the room already made, so there is nothing to poll: the
# node settles on the link and the call itself happens between the page and Tavus.
- name: start
  method: POST
  url: https://tavusapi.com/v2/conversations

  credential:
    scheme: apiKeyHeader
    header: x-api-key
    value: "{{ credentials.tavusCredential.apiKey }}"

  # BUILT, not mutated: each optional field is left out when empty, because Tavus reads an empty
  # face id or greeting as a value rather than as "use the PAL's own".
  body: |
    return Object.assign(
      {
        pal_id: config.palId,
        properties: {
          max_call_duration: config.maxCallDuration,
          participant_left_timeout: config.participantLeftTimeout,
          participant_absent_timeout: config.participantAbsentTimeout
        }
      },
      config.faceId ? { face_id: config.faceId } : {},
      config.conversationalContext ? { conversational_context: config.conversationalContext } : {},
      config.customGreeting ? { custom_greeting: config.customGreeting } : {},
      config.testMode ? { test_mode: true } : {}
    );

  timeoutMs: 30000

  # NOT 400. Tavus answers 400 when the account is at its concurrent-call limit, and starting the
  # same call again would only open a second one once the first frees up.
  retry:
    attempts: 3
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]

  transport: json

  error:
    when: "return !response.conversation_url"
    message: "return response.message || response.error || 'Tavus returned no conversation link'"
files.config.yaml:
configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [palId]
  properties:
    palId:
      type: string
      title: PAL ID
      description: The PAL who takes the call, from your Tavus dashboard. It sets the voice, behaviour and tools.
    faceId:
      type: string
      title: Face ID
      description: The face to show. Leave empty to use the PAL's own face.
      default: ""
    conversationalContext:
      type: string
      title: Context
      description: What this call is about, added to the PAL's own context. Usually wired in from an upstream node.
      default: ""
      ui:field: template
    customGreeting:
      type: string
      title: Greeting
      description: The first thing the face says once someone joins. Leave empty for the PAL's own greeting.
      default: ""
      ui:field: template
    maxCallDuration:
      type: number
      title: Longest call (seconds)
      description: The call ends at this length whatever is happening, so a forgotten tab stops costing.
      default: 600
      minimum: 10
      maximum: 3600
    participantLeftTimeout:
      type: number
      title: End after leaving (seconds)
      description: How long the call stays open once the person has left.
      default: 30
      minimum: 0
      maximum: 3600
    participantAbsentTimeout:
      type: number
      title: End if nobody joins (seconds)
      description: How long the call waits for the person to join before it closes.
      default: 120
      minimum: 10
      maximum: 3600
    testMode:
      type: boolean
      title: Test mode
      description: Creates the call without the face joining, so nothing is charged.
      default: false
      ui:widget: toggle

ui:order:
  [palId, faceId, conversationalContext, customGreeting, maxCallDuration, participantLeftTimeout, participantAbsentTimeout, testMode]

files.node.yaml:
type: TavusConversation
kind: PromiseNode

name: Tavus Conversation
category: Voice
color: "#5B3DF5"

description: Starts a live video conversation with an AI face and returns its link

whenToUse: >-
  Pick when someone should talk face to face with an AI: a live video call where a talking face
  listens, sees and answers in real time. The call runs on the video service with the persona and
  tools configured there, so the workflow starts it and hands back the link rather than writing
  each reply. Wire the link to a component that shows the call.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # A new call every run: never served from a previous one.
  cacheable: false
  # A CHARGE. Every conversation is billed from the moment the face joins, and that cannot be
  # taken back. Canvas test runs therefore withhold this node; the Nodes screen in studio still
  # runs it for real, and `testMode` there starts a call with no face and no charge.
  emitsExternally: true
files.test.yaml:
# TEST MODE, so a run makes the room and no face joins: no charge. It reaches the real API, so it
# needs TAVUS_API_KEY in your .env and a PAL id from your own dashboard in place of the one below.
testData:
  config:
    palId: p0000000000
    conversationalContext: The person wants a short tour of what the platform does.
    maxCallDuration: 60
    participantLeftTimeout: 10
    participantAbsentTimeout: 60
    testMode: true
  inputs:
    signal:
      topic: A short tour of the platform
  expect:
    conversationUrl: "return typeof output.conversationUrl === 'string' && output.conversationUrl.startsWith('https://')"
    conversationId: "return typeof output.conversationId === 'string' && output.conversationId.length > 0"
